title: SLA-driven locality routing and soft-degrade orchestration for ranking service
creator: Marcus Li
description: Improve the ranking/rerank endpoint so it can maintain P95 latency SLOs under regional degradation and burst traffic. Deliverables: (1) SLA-driven locality routing that prefers local replicas but expands fanout when headroom is available, (2) a configurable circuit-breaker layer with tiered thresholds and timeout inheritance, (3) soft-degrade policies that automatically switch to cached or lower-cost model variants for low-priority requests, and (4) telemetry and dashboards to verify behavior across scales. Goal: reduce P95 tail latency by 30% during cross-region incidents while keeping cost uplift <10% in normal traffic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P95 latency for high-priority rerank requests in the eu-west region remains <120ms during simulated eu-west capacity loss (test harness). 2) Circuit breaker trips and recovers according to policy with no more than 1% request loss for P0 customers. 3) Canary rollout to 10% of traffic shows graceful fallback to cached embeddings with output-quality regression <1.5% measured on benchmark set. 4) New metrics (regional_fanout, cb_state, degrade_mode) are emitted and wired into console dashboards.
implementation_notes: We will implement a routing policy that weights local replicas by recent SLO headroom and penalizes cross-region fanout when latency increases. Circuit breaker decisions use a sliding-window error+latency score rather than pure failure rate to better reflect QPS spikes. Timeout inheritance: if frontdoor gives a 300ms budget and downstream ranking has staged timeouts (50ms fast, 200ms slow), we propagate reduced budgets to attempt cached/local fast paths first. Soft-degrade uses model family fallbacks (e.g., reranker-lite -> reranker-quant) plus cached embedding lookup. Configs will be per-customer and per-route with sane defaults.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in staging with synthetic traffic profiles (10 days). 2) Canary at 2% on dedicated infra with traffic shadowing for 48 hours. 3) Canary to 10% with active monitoring for 72 hours. 4) Incremental roll to 50% and then global after automated verification. Emergency killswitch documented in runbook.
test_plan: - Synthetic fault injection: partial region failure, delayed responses, connection drops. - Regression test: ranking quality on benchmark dataset (QPS 500 baseline). - Load test: 2x peak QPS for 1 hour to validate circuit thresholds and autoscaling interactions. - Chaos: random node reboots during canary.
observability_changes: Add metrics: rerank.local_headroom_pct, rerank.regional_fanout_count, rerank.cb_state{route,region}, rerank.degrade_mode. Add traces for routing decision and degrade path. Dashboard: rerank-slo-overview and rerank-degrade-events. Alerting: adapt existing SLO alert to include degrade-mode rate >5%.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-eager degrade reduces quality. Mitigation: conservative thresholds in first canaries and automated rollback on quality regression >2%. Risk: cost increase during long cross-region fanout. Mitigation: cap fanout budget and prioritize cached/quant variants. Risk: config complexity for customers. Mitigation: sensible defaults and UI presets in console.
